resolutions.title: The `pr:` reader's inert-value warnings are unreachable — no engine path calls them, and the reference misattributes them
resolutions.resolution: A — give the reader a consumer the bodies invoke; surface the resolved regime on the orientation surface

options_presented.label: A
options_presented.body: Surface the resolved mode through a read-only CLI the bodies invoke.

options_presented.label: B
options_presented.body: Delete the reader; move inert-detection into the reference as the body's job.

options_presented.label: C
options_presented.body: Keep both and fix only the false attribution.

resolutions.action: `Orientation` gained a `pr: PrMode` field resolved via `readProjectConfig` + `resolvePrMode`, surfaced on BOTH JSON tiers of the bare orientation surface (sprint and full). The shared reference and both body pointers now instruct: read the RESOLVED regime from `orbit status --json`, field `pr` — never parse `orbit/config.yaml` yourself — with the reason stated inline: the value set is CLOSED and every failure path inert, so a body parsing YAML would re-derive that resolution in prose, quietly accepting a typo the reader rejects and never emitting the promised warning. The false attribution is gone; the reference now says any config warning already came from the reader and must not be restated. Chose A over deleting the reader because this change uses engine-computes/body-reads everywhere else (gates, position, emits, boot) and this converts the closed-set enforcement from a promise into something that actually happens. Six orientation tests cover it, including that an unrecognized value and the superseded two-key block both resolve to `never` — the typo never reaches the choreography — and that a malformed config never throws.

resolutions.title: Touchpoints omits `pr-choreography.ts`, the change's one new source file, and freezes at the first apply commit
resolutions.action: Added the entry to the predicted map, describing the file as the single source for the shared resolution, propose phases, and archive tail emitted as a `references/` file into all three seams. Verified via `orbit status --change d6-pr-lifecycle --boot --json` that `predicted` now carries it (13 entries). Applied inside the freeze window deliberately: `touchpoints.actual` is still null because no apply work is committed, and the section becomes unamendable from the first apply commit — so this was the last moment it could be fixed rather than carried as a permanent false positive at every audit-drift category-5 sweep.

resolutions.title: Scaffolding residue in the new harness fixture: a no-op git call and a CommonJS require in an ESM module
resolutions.action: Deleted the discarded `rev-parse --show-toplevel` probe (a subprocess per invocation that read as meaningful) and hoisted `spawnSync` to a top-level import, matching every other module in the repo. 28 harness cases still pass.

final_assessment: 3 of 3 resolved; 0 unresolved markers in scope. One decision-lane finding ratified in chat toward connecting the engine surface rather than deleting it: the resolved `pr` regime is now a field on the orientation surface that the bodies read, so the closed value set is enforced once by the reader instead of re-derived in prose at three seams — and the reference no longer claims warnings come from a reader nothing invoked. The Touchpoints entry landed inside the freeze window, which closes at the first apply commit. Both warnings were the same shape the review named: implementation correct in isolation, not connected. 1988 -> 1996 tests green across 91 files; five parity hashes re-pinned after verifying only the three edited templates changed (32 unchanged).
